title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis dormancy regulon proteins Rv2627c and Rv2628 as Toll like receptor agonist and as potential adjuvant.
authors: Bhatt, Parul; Sharma, Monika; Prakash Sharma, Prem; Rathi, Brijesh; Sharma, Sadhna
one_liner_zh: 该文研究结核分枝杆菌休眠蛋白Rv2627c/Rv2628作为TLR激动剂佐剂，虽含分子对接模拟，但核心是免疫佐剂功能而非TF-DNA互作，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: During latency, DosR proteins of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) get activated and help the bacterium to remain dormant. We have shown earlier that 2 such proteins Rv2627c and Rv2628 are immunogenic and induce a TH1 kind of immune response. In this study, through in-vitro experiments we have confirmed that Rv2627c and Rv2628 proteins act as protein Toll-Like Receptor (TLR) agonist-adjuvant. Rv2627c and Rv2628 stimulated THP-1 macrophages showed an increased expression of TLR2, TLR4 and co-stimulatory molecules CD40, CD80, CD86 and antigen presenting molecule HLA-DR. Further studies also found enhanced expression of downstream signaling molecules of TLR activation like MyD88, NF-kappaB-p65 and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Inhibition studies using TLR blocking antibodies decreased the expression of co-stimulatory molecules, MyD88, NF-kappaB-p65, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Rv2627c and Rv2628 stimulation of HEK-TLR2 reporter cell line confirmed the interaction of these proteins with TLR2. Moreover, molecular docking and simulations of Rv2627c and Rv2628 proteins with TLR2 and TLR4 showed stable interactions. The adjuvant activity of Rv2628 was further validated by a protein adjuvanted with pre-clinically validated peptides as multi-epitope vaccine construct which showed good binding with TLR2 and TLR4 and activate dendritic cells and induce sustained pro-inflammatory cytokine response by C-ImmSim analysis. We propose that our vaccine construct will produce a better immune response than BCG and can be taken up as a post-exposure therapeutic subunit vaccine along with standard TB therapy. We also anticipate that our construct can be taken up as a protein adjuvant with other vaccine candidates as these can activate macrophages through TLR signaling.
abstract_zh: 在潜伏期，结核分枝杆菌（Mycobacterium tuberculosis, M.tb）的DosR蛋白被激活，帮助细菌保持休眠状态。我们此前已表明，其中两种蛋白Rv2627c和Rv2628具有免疫原性，并能诱导TH1型免疫应答。在本研究中，通过体外实验，我们确认Rv2627c和Rv2628蛋白作为蛋白类Toll样受体（Toll-Like Receptor, TLR）激动剂-佐剂发挥作用。Rv2627c和Rv2628刺激的THP-1巨噬细胞显示出TLR2、TLR4及共刺激分子CD40、CD80、CD86和抗原呈递分子HLA-DR的表达增加。进一步研究还发现，TLR激活的下游信号分子如MyD88、NF-kappaB-p65及促炎细胞因子的表达增强。使用TLR阻断抗体的抑制实验降低了共刺激分子、MyD88、NF-kappaB-p65及促炎细胞因子的表达。Rv2627c和Rv2628刺激HEK-TLR2报告细胞系证实了这些蛋白与TLR2的相互作用。此外，Rv2627c和Rv2628蛋白与TLR2和TLR4的分子对接和模拟显示稳定相互作用。Rv2628的佐剂活性进一步通过一种蛋白佐剂与临床前验证肽作为多表位疫苗构建体得到验证，该构建体与TLR2和TLR4表现出良好结合，并能激活树突状细胞，通过C-ImmSim分析诱导持续的促炎细胞因子反应。我们提出，我们的疫苗构建体将比BCG产生更好的免疫应答，并可作为暴露后治疗性亚单位疫苗与标准结核病治疗联合使用。我们还预期，我们的构建体可作为蛋白佐剂与其他疫苗候选物一起使用，因为这些蛋白能通过TLR信号激活巨噬细胞。
